edition.title: Week of Oct 19, 2026
edition.note: Each item was checked on its official page on Oct 22, 2026. Items without a verifiable date or free access were left out.

items.creator: Mel Robbins
items.title: How to Unlock Your Full Potential with Adam Grant (Episode 448)
items.summary: Organizational psychologist Adam Grant talks with Mel Robbins about potential as the capacity to grow, and about overthinking, confidence, feedback, relationships and career skills.
items.why: Touches on overthinking and confidence, which often get in the way of following through.

claims.text: The episode frames potential as how much you grow rather than where you start. This is the guest’s framework; the episode page itself doesn’t cite studies.

items.creator: Tim Ferriss
items.title: Q&A with Tim: The 4-Hour Workweek in a World of AI, Rebuilding Personal Agency, and More (#887)
items.summary: A listener Q&A on applying The 4-Hour Workweek with AI tools, rebuilding momentum, persistence versus quitting, friendships and serendipity.
items.why: Covers rebuilding momentum and deciding when to persist or quit, which matter when goals compete.
items.disclosure: The episode notes list sponsors (Incogni, Our Place, Momentous and AG1). One Day has no relationship with any of them.

claims.text: Advice in a Q&A is the host’s personal experience and opinion.

items.creator: James Clear
items.title: 3-2-1: On refusing to give up, the refrains of nature, and making things fun
items.summary: Three short ideas on choices, tolerating brief discomfort and what success looks like, with quotes from Rachel Carson and Marcus Aurelius and a question about turning a task into something enjoyable.
items.why: The closing question about making a task fun fits creativity and enjoyment, and refusing to give up fits following through.

claims.text: These are the author’s reflections and selected quotes, not research findings.

items.creator: Steven Bartlett
items.title: Phone Addiction Scientist: Doing This Gives You An Hour Back Every Day! (Dr Sahar Yousef)
items.summary: Steven Bartlett and Dr. Sahar Yousef discuss digital distraction, attention, phone habits, multitasking and boredom.
items.why: Practical focus habits can protect the short daily blocks your plan depends on.
items.disclosure: The episode description lists sponsors (Ketone and LinkedIn Talent Solutions). One Day has no relationship with them.

claims.text: The description says multitasking “makes you up to 60% slower” and that grayscale mode “significantly reduces neurological stimulation.” No study is cited for either figure, so treat them as unverified.
The title’s promise of “an hour back every day” is a headline, not a measured result.

items.creator: James Clear
items.title: 3-2-1: On staying in the game, the power of best practices, and how to handle bad events
items.summary: Argues that dwelling on past mistakes costs present opportunities, and suggests starting from established practices in a field and adapting them to your situation.
items.why: Starting from best practices is a practical way to shape a new data analytics service; staying in the game fits sustainable discipline.

items.creator: Mel Robbins
items.title: The Best Financial Advice You’ll Ever Hear, with Morgan Housel (Episode 327)
items.summary: Author Morgan Housel and Mel Robbins discuss how people earn, save and invest, and which habits keep people in financial difficulty. Mel describes paying off about $800,000 of debt.

claims.text: General ideas and personal stories, not financial advice for your situation.

tryOne.title: Make one avoided task 10% more enjoyable
tryOne.text: Pick one task you’ve been putting off this week. Change one detail to make it more pleasant, like music, a different spot or a small treat after, then do just 10 minutes of it.
tryOne.connection: The newsletter closes with a question about how a task would look if it were fun.
tryOne.finish: Ten minutes done, with one detail changed.
